I'm using a pair of Audio Technica ATH-M50s I bought a few years back. They're sweet.

Any good pair of headphones (not some trendy/fashion victim shit like Beats or Skullcandy) will be good. Any "bass enhancing" headphones are garbage, IMO. I will never understand that shit. I like to hear music how it was intended to be heard, by the artist, if possible (it can be difficult these days with older music, with all of the remastering that goes on). At the very least, I don't fuck with the mix on the album by passing it through an EQ to boost certain frequencies.

I have a pair of AKG 240s headphones. Great sounding, relatively cheap (~$60 USD, on Amazon) headphones, that will last years (had mine for close to 10 years now, and they still work great). They are good "workhorse" headphones, which is probably partly why they are still used in a lot of studios today, even though they were designed in the 70s. But if you care most about having lots of (too much) low end, then they are definitely not for you. They are relatively light on the bass.

But to each their own. You can listen to music however the shit you like, my friend, as long as it makes you happy (or even if it doesn't, but I wouldn't suggest it). I'm just a hater. Don't listen to me—except for the part about investing in some good headphones.

For one thing, they need to stop being so long. The downside to YouTube and moving away from the previous 30 second advertisements have really harmed films.

Giving me a 5 minute video that gives me a synopsis of the beginning, middle, and end of the plot points, along with snippets of every punch line so every joke is ruined, and spoiling all the surprises makes it pointless to see the movie. The only thing left is all the CGI and a complete inability to build tension.

This is made worse by all the remakes that aren't even trying to break new ground. Showcasing every single minute detail that separates it from the original before the movie is even released defeats the purpose of bothering to pay money to watch it when you've already seen the (likely superior) original.

If it's an action movie, just show us ONE of the scenes in which the main character is a badass. If it's a comedy, show us the build up and finish of ONE of the better jokes, and sell it off of that. Maybe two. If it's a drama, have a narrator give us a synopsis of the struggle.

But stop showing us the entire movie. Give us a teaser, an appetizer, stop giving us the main course for free and then hoping we'll want dessert.
